rationale: Six attempts observed. Best is attempt-03 at 156.26us (block_M=64,block_N=64,block_K=64,stages=2,threads=128,swizzle=4, smem=32768, 3 blocks/SM). attempt-05 and attempt-06 both simulated 156.49us (block_M=64,block_N=128,block_K=64, stages=1, threads=256, swizzle 8 then 4), essentially tied; attempts-00=157.29us; attempts-01/02=186.64us identically across swizzle 16 vs 64, confirming the small-tile/short-K regime is worse and large panels give no measurable gain here. All passed numerics/SMT and compiled. Latencies cluster tightly (~156-157us) for block_K=64, so block_K=64 is the competitive regime. Revision: previous attempt-06 dropped block_K=128, but the last two MIP rounds have repeatedly landed on the same block_K=64/stage=1-2/threads=256 near-tie; to break the plateau I reopen block_K=32 and block_N=32 (feasibility slack under the 32768 cap) while keeping block_K=64, and re-add threads=64 (unmeasured, a genuine warp-layout probe distinct from the 128-vs-256 tie). Keep block_M 64/128 and block_N up to 256 to test wider-N launch reduction. Swizzle reopened to full [0,4,8,16,32,64] but M=128 gives at most 2 tile rows for block_M=64, so panel gains are hypothesized small; instruction warns large panels may exceed cache, so lean on measured feedback rather than proxy. Weights held near prior (traffic/launches/pipeline 1.2, footprint 0.5) since footprint is pinned at cap and not the limiter. Shared limit stays 32768 (hard portability cap binds). Next hypothesis: test thread=64 and block_K=32 viability plus stage=3-4 at block_K=64 to see if any tuple beats 156.26us; if the plateau persists, accept the block_K=64 regime as the local floor. Validation scope: Metal executes exact source/config/TIR numerics; CUDA binary not executed; GB10 latencies are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; no global optimality claimed.
